Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

health noun

also good health, bad health, be healthy, be well, look after your health

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē
Traupman 64

valētūdō, valētūdinis f.

noun, third declension

health, good or bad

On its own it can mean either; bona valētūdō is good health, adversa, mala, īnfirma valētūdō ill health (Traupman 64). How someone is goes with the verb: valeō, I’m well; valētūdinem cūrāre, to look after one’s health.

Examples

  • sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō. valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē

    if you are well, good; I am well. Please look after your health with the greatest careCic. Fam. 14.8.1

  • valētūdō sustentātur nōtitiā suī corporis et observātiōne, quae rēs aut prōdesse soleant aut obesse

    health is kept up by knowing one’s own body and noticing what usually does it good or harmCic. Off. 2.86

  • ipse melior fīō, prīmum valētūdine, quam intermissīs exercitātiōnibus āmīseram

    I am getting better myself: first in health, which I had lost by giving up my exerciseCic. Fam. 9.18.3

  • nōn est vīvere, sed valēre vīta est

    life is not just being alive, but being wellMart. 6.70.15

Other words

  • valeō, valēre, valuī, valitum — be well, be in good health

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō

    The verb Latin prefers: ut valēs?, how are you?; cūrā ut valeās, look after yourself.

  • sānitās, sānitātis f. — health, soundness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 678–679: salūtem et sānitātem nostrae familiae; Cic. Tusc. 4.30 (Lewis & Short)

    Soundness of body; in Cicero also soundness of mind.

  • sānus, sāna, sānum — healthy, sound, well (of a person)

    also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.1.108: praecipuē sānus, nisi cum pītuīta molesta est

    Food that is good for you is salūbris (see healthy).

  • salūs, salūtis f. — health, welfare, safety

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 141.3: bonam salūtem valētūdinemque (Lewis & Short)

    Wider than valētūdō: wellbeing and safety; also the greeting of a letter (salūtem dīcere).

See also healthy, ill, I don’t feel well, body, life.
